<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game using its dependency-free browser systems.
- Add chapter progression with a night-7 boss and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable.
- Improve map, character, companion, shelter, and creature visuals; add varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection.
- Support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `capture.sh`.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay, visual, menu, shelter-entry, and mobile improvements.
- Test night-7 boss behavior and the chapter/region transition.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the requested gameplay, menu, shelter-entry, visual, and mobile changes.
2. Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition.
3. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification results and briefly note implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, world generation, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. `beginNextDay()` advances chapters every eight survived nights; `advanceChapter()` may randomly collapse one shelter. No night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates; terrain and resources use seeded generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons. Touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Field-kit UI has close controls, but inspected input bindings did not show kit open/close handling.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game using its dependency-free browser systems.
- Add chapter progression with a night-7 boss and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable.
- Improve map, character, companion, shelter, and creature visuals; add varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection.
- Support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `capture.sh`.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay, visual, menu, shelter-entry, and mobile improvements.
- Test night-7 boss behavior and the chapter/region transition.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the requested gameplay, menu, shelter-entry, visual, and mobile changes.
2. Test the night-7 boss and the chapter/region transition.
3. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification results and briefly note implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, world generation, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `git status --short` and `git diff --stat` showed no existing changes.
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. `beginNextDay()` advances chapters every eight survived nights; `advanceChapter()` may randomly collapse one shelter. No night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates; terrain and resources use seeded generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons. Touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Field-kit UI has close controls, but inspected input bindings did not show kit open/close handling.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game using its dependency-free browser systems.
- Add chapter progression with a night-7 boss and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable.
- Improve map, character, companion, shelter, and creature visuals; add varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection.
- Support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `capture.sh`, and `README.md`.
- Mapped gameplay insertion points for world/chapter progression, enemy lifecycle, shelter interactions, and input/UI handling.

### Active
- Implement the requested gameplay, visual, menu, shelter-entry, and mobile improvements.
- Test night-7 boss behavior and the chapter/region transition.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the requested gameplay, menu, shelter-entry, visual, and mobile changes.
2. Test the night-7 boss and the chapter/region transition.
3. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification results and briefly note implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, world generation, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. `beginNextDay()` advances chapters every eight survived nights; `advanceChapter()` may randomly collapse one shelter. No night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates; terrain and resources use seeded generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons. Touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Field-kit UI has close controls, but inspected input bindings did not show kit open/close handling.
- Key implementation locations: `buildWorld()` and `resetRun()`; `beginNextDay()` and `advanceChapter()`; enemy spawn helpers, `updateEnemies()`, and `drawEnemy()`; `updateInteraction()` and `doInteract()`; `bindInput()`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game using its dependency-free browser systems.
- Add chapter progression with a night-7 boss and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable.
- Improve map, character, companion, shelter, and creature visuals; add varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection.
- Support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `capture.sh` to locate relevant gameplay and UI systems.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay, visual, menu, shelter-entry, and mobile improvements.
- Test night-7 boss behavior and the chapter/region transition.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the requested gameplay, menu, shelter-entry, visual, and mobile changes.
2. Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition.
3. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification results and briefly note implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, world generation, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. `beginNextDay()` advances chapters every eight survived nights; `advanceChapter()` may randomly collapse one shelter. No night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates; terrain and resources use seeded generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons. Touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Field-kit UI has close controls, but inspected input bindings did not show kit open/close handling.
- Key implementation locations: `buildWorld()` and `resetRun()`; `beginNextDay()` and `advanceChapter()`; enemy spawn helpers, `updateEnemies()`, and `drawEnemy()`; `updateInteraction()` and `doInteract()`; `bindInput()`.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game with chapter progression, a night-7 boss, and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable; improve visuals for the map, character, companion, shelter, and varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection and support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
- Briefly note reasonable implementation assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game lifecycle, chapter progression, enemy spawning/rendering, shelter interaction, input, and HUD systems.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay and visual changes in `game.js`.
- A subagent is working on menu and responsive/mobile UI changes in `index.html` and `styles.css`; changes are not yet confirmed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementation, coordinating the gameplay changes with pending UI work.
2. Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition.
3. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification results and briefly note implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. `beginNextDay()` advances chapters every eight survived nights; `advanceChapter()` may randomly collapse one shelter. No night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates; terrain and resources use seeded generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons. Touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Field-kit UI has close controls, but inspected input bindings did not show kit open/close handling.

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game with chapter progression, a night-7 boss, and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable; improve visuals for the map, character, companion, shelter, and varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection and support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
- Briefly note reasonable implementation assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `README.md`, and `capture.sh` to inspect the existing game.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay and visual changes.
- Verify menu closability/minimization and responsive mobile UI.
- Test the boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the boss, region-specific transition/map, shelter entry/protection, and requested visual improvements.
2. Verify and improve menu closability/minimization and responsive mobile UI.
3. Test night 7 and the chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification and reasonable implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. Chapter advancement occurs every eight survived nights; no night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is confirmed implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates and seeded terrain/resource generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons; touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Menu HTML includes a checkbox/label minimizer, but closability and behavior still need verification.
- No gameplay edits or test/capture results are confirmed.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game with chapter progression, a night-7 boss, and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable; improve visuals for the map, character, companion, shelter, and varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection and support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
- Briefly note reasonable implementation assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `README.md`, and `capture.sh`.

### Active
- Implement requested gameplay and visual changes.
- Verify menu closability/minimization and responsive mobile UI.
- Test night 7 and the chapter/region transition; capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the boss, region-specific transition/map, shelter entry/protection, and requested visual improvements.
2. Verify and improve menu closability/minimization and responsive mobile UI.
3. Test night 7 and the chapter/region transition; capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification and reasonable implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. Chapter advancement occurs every eight survived nights; no night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is confirmed implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates and seeded terrain/resource generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons; touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Menu HTML includes a checkbox/label minimizer, but closability and behavior still need verification.
- No gameplay edits or test/capture results are confirmed.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

I checked the local runtime and browser tooling that’s actually available here, and this project is set up as a static HTML game, not a Node/Vite app.

What’s available

- Browser runtime:
  - Chromium installed at `/usr/bin/google-chrome`
  - Chrome driver at `/usr/bin/chromedriver`
  - Firefox installed too
- Playwright tooling:
  - `/usr/local/bin/playwright-cli`
  - config at `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`
  - display/Xvfb setup under `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/`
- Runtime scripts:
  - `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`
  - `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`

The game itself is a static app containing `index.html`, so the default launcher is a simple local static server.

Launch commands

1. Start the local preview server:
   - `cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`
   - `export RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`
   - `./start.sh`

This resolves to:
- `node "${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-start.mjs"`
- which serves the project root on port 3000 by default, unless `PORT` is set.

You can also launch it directly:
- `cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`
- `PORT=3000 RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime node /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`

Expected URL:
- `http://localhost:3000`

Capture commands

There are two relevant paths:

A. Use the project helper:
- `cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`
- `export RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`
- `export CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000`
- `export CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/game-captures`
- `mkdir -p "$CAPTURE_DIR"`
- `./capture.sh`

This resolves to:
- `node "${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-capture.mjs"`

B. Use the preconfigured Playwright browser directly:
- `mkdir -p /tmp/game-captures`
- `DISPLAY=:$(cat /home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/display) playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000`
- `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=/tmp/game-captures/linux.png`

Constraints and environment details

- The runtime expects a preconfigured headed Chromium session with Xvfb.
- `playwright-cli` is the approved tool here, not ad hoc Selenium or custom browser scripts.
- The Chromium launch config is explicitly set to use SwiftShader:
  - `--use-vulkan=swiftshader`
  - `--use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader`
- That means:
  - WebGPU is enabled in software rendering mode
  - do not claim hardware GPU acceleration
  - report it as SwiftShader / CPU software rendering
- The capture script automatically tests both:
  - desktop: 1440x900
  - mobile: 390x844
  and saves:
  - `final-desktop.png`
  - `final-mobile.png`

Important caveats

- `./start.sh` and `./capture.sh` require `RUNTIME_DIR` to be set in the environment.
- `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR` are required for the capture script.
- The project has no package.json or Vite build process, so this is not a normal Node app startup flow; it is a static HTML preview being served by the runtime harness.
- If the page is blank or not ready, capture will fail because the browser waits for visible body content and fonts to load before taking the screenshot.

Short version

Use:
- `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh`
- then either:
  - `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/game-captures RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./capture.sh`
  - or `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000` followed by a screenshot command

This is the supported local test/capture path in this environment.

## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game with chapter progression, a night-7 boss, and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable; improve visuals for the map, character, companion, shelter, and varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection and support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
- Briefly note reasonable implementation assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected game state, chapter progression, shelter/enemy systems, rendering, and menu/input code.
- Confirmed browser testing and capture tools are available; no gameplay edits or test/capture results are confirmed.

### Active
- Implement the boss, region-specific transition/map, shelter entry/protection, and requested visual improvements.
- Verify menu closability/minimization and responsive mobile UI.
- Test night 7 and the chapter/region transition; capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the boss and chapter/region transition, shelter entry/protection, and requested visual/UI improvements.
2. Verify menu and mobile behavior.
3. Test night 7 and the chapter/region transition; capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
4. Report verification and reasonable implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, shelters, enemies, chapter progression, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries. Chapter advancement occurs every eight survived nights; no night-7 boss or region-specific map transition is confirmed implemented.
- World dimensions are fixed at 3000×2200 with hard-coded shelter coordinates and seeded terrain/resource generation.
- Existing enemies are `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation, but not player entry/protection.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons; touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing and resuming. Menu HTML includes a checkbox/label minimizer, but closability and behavior still need verification.
- Browser preview uses `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh`; capture uses `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/game-captures RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./capture.sh`. The provided capture helper saves desktop/mobile PNGs; the requested JPEG still needs to be produced and inspected.
- Browser runtime uses SwiftShader/CPU software rendering.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Nightfall into a detailed, playable SCP survival game with chapter progression, a night-7 boss, and a region-specific map after defeating it.

## Requirements
- Make the menu closable and minimizable; improve visuals for the map, character, companion, shelter, and varied, stronger SCP-like creatures.
- Let the player enter shelters for protection and support mobile gameplay with a mobile-friendly layout.
- Keep the game dependency-free and extend existing systems.
- Test the night-7 boss and chapter/region transition; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
- Briefly note reasonable implementation assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Use chapter progression with a region-specific map and a night-7 boss.
- Preserve and extend existing chapter, shelter, companion, enemy, and touch-control systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected existing progression, UI, rendering, shelters, enemies, and capture/start scripts.
- Added a menu visibility checkbox and minimize/restore label in `index.html`, with initial styling in `styles.css`; behavior remains unverified.

### Active
- Implement the night-7 boss, region transition/map, and shelter entry/protection.
- Improve visual variety and verify menu behavior and responsive mobile UI.
- Test progression and capture/inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js` progression, shelter, input, and rendering symbols before editing.
2. Implement the boss, region-specific transition/map, shelter protection, and visual/UI improvements.
3. Run and verify night-7 and post-boss progression.
4. Capture and inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.
5. Report results and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Progression, shelters, enemies, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, menu, overlays, shelter panel, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Menu and responsive/mobile styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: Browser game server startup.
- `README.md`: Project/game documentation.

## Important Context
- `CHAPTER_NIGHTS` is `8`; `CHAPTERS` contains six entries; no confirmed night-7 boss or region-specific map transition.
- World dimensions are `3000×2200`; shelters use hard-coded coordinates and seeded terrain/resource generation.
- Existing enemies: `walker`, `crawler`, `brute`, and `wraith`.
- Shelters support claiming, fortification, companion sheltering, raids, barricade damage, and haunt escalation; player entry/protection is unconfirmed.
- Touch controls include joystick, USE, and FIRE buttons; touch mode is detected through `(pointer: coarse)` and `body.touch`.
- `togglePause()` supports pausing/resuming. Menu checkbox behavior and closability are unverified.
- `index.html` and `styles.css` are modified and uncommitted; `git status --short` showed no `game.js` modification.
- Browser preview: `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh`.
- Capture: `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/game-captures RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./capture.sh`; JPEG conversion/inspection remains pending.
